questions.q: Which two things must a flow have before it can be added to an agent as a tool?
options: An HTTP trigger and a Parse JSON action
A scheduled trigger and an Approvals action
The "When an agent calls the flow" trigger and a "Respond to the agent" action
A SharePoint trigger and a Compose action
questions.explain: A flow must have the dedicated "When an agent calls the flow" trigger plus a "Respond to the agent" action that hands its result back to the calling agent.

questions.q: Why must a flow attached to an agent respond within roughly 100 seconds and with the Asynchronous response toggle off?
options: Because Power Automate bills by the second for any flow over 100 seconds
Because the agent is waiting synchronously on the other end of the call for the flow's result
Because Copilot Studio agents cannot run for more than 100 seconds total in their lifetime
This is not actually a real requirement
questions.explain: The agent calls the flow and waits for a synchronous response to continue the conversation, so the flow must respond quickly — within the 100-second action limit — rather than asynchronously.

questions.q: What is the difference between an agent-level tool and a topic-level tool?
options: There is no difference; both terms describe the same thing
An agent-level tool can only be used by administrators, while a topic-level tool can be used by any employee
An agent-level tool is available to the orchestrator for any relevant request; a topic-level tool is scoped to one specific topic's conversation path
A topic-level tool runs faster than an agent-level tool
questions.explain: Agent-level tools can be called by the orchestrator whenever it judges them relevant across the whole agent. Topic-level tools are only available within the specific topic they were added to.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize writing a clear description when attaching a flow as a tool?
options: Descriptions are purely cosmetic and don't affect agent behavior
The agent's orchestrator reads the tool's description to decide when it's the right tool to call for a given request
The description is only shown to the person who built the flow, never to end users or the agent
A description is required only for topic-level tools, never for agent-level tools
questions.explain: The orchestrator uses the tool's description (along with its name and parameters) to decide whether to call it for a given user request — a vague description leads to the tool not being selected when it should be.

questions.q: In the real Copilot Studio designer screenshot shown in this lesson, what pattern does the example "Customer feedback triage" flow use?
options: A single linear sequence of actions with no branching
A trigger, an AI step that summarizes and assigns a category, then a branch that routes to different teams by category
A flow that only sends an email and does nothing else
A flow with no trigger, started manually by an administrator every time
questions.explain: The example flow has a trigger, an AI summarization/categorization step, and a branching action that routes the result to different teams — structurally similar to the ticket-triage capstone later in this chapter.
